title: CRITICAL: the worker green-start probe times out before a real container can boot
description:
Found by the first real per-tick container wave, run_1ce4fae5 on 2026-08-22. The wave was written off in 21 seconds:

  06:38:49.641  dispatched
  06:38:52.781  cloud_wave:width=3:capped
  06:39:13.985  cloud_reconcile:1:3 never-dispatched
  06:39:14.098  handoff:closeout

All three worker manifests were written with a real process_id and dispatched_at, so containers WERE addressed — then reconcile classified 3 of 3 as never-dispatched and collect correctly reported no-commits ("tick/72y/3nh does not exist on origin"). The run fell back to closeout under the Phase 1 single-sandbox path.

Cause: DEFAULT_PROBE_TIMEOUT_MS is 30s and DEFAULT_CONFIRM_TIMEOUT_MS is 60s, but kuf measured a COLD container start at 93.2 seconds, of which 71.9s is the image pull. A cold worker cannot answer a probe inside 30s, so the green-start trap fires on every cold container and reports the honest-but-wrong verdict "this container started cleanly and did nothing".

This is the exact class Phase 1 paid for and the final review predicted: the timeouts look generous against FakeSandboxes, which answers instantly, and are impossible against a real Cloudflare Sandbox pulling a 1.1 GB compressed image. 532 green tests could not see it. Note the numbers to fix it were already committed in this same epic — kuf measured them, and nothing connected the benchmark to the timeout.

Fix: size the probe and confirm budgets from measured cold start with headroom, not from a round number; distinguish "still booting" from "booted and did nothing" so the green-start trap keeps its meaning; and add a guard test that asserts the probe budget exceeds the committed cold-start benchmark, so the two cannot drift apart again.
